name: Velthar-Prime
description: Velthar-Prime stretches endlessly beneath a pale amber sky, its rust-colored dust seas broken only by the jagged walls of canyon systems that plunge kilometers into darkness. The largest crater, known as the Maw, spans two hundred kilometers and catches the light of the distant sun in ways that make it visible from orbit. Wind-sculpted ridges ripple across the plains like frozen waves, their edges honed sharp by eons of particle bombardment.

The thin atmosphere carries a perpetual whisper of fine particles, creating an eerie background hiss that fills every silence. Temperature swings from frigid nights to scorching days stress equipment and test endurance. The canyons offer shelter from the worst of the thermal extremes, their depths holding onto cold long after the surface bakes.

Mining consortiums operated here for decades, extracting titanium from the canyon walls until the veins ran thin and corporate interest moved elsewhere. The abandoned processing facilities still stand, their skeletal frames slowly being buried by advancing dust. More puzzling is the distress beacon that began transmitting three years after the last workers departed—a signal no one has claimed, broadcasting from coordinates that show nothing but empty dust.

Salvagers occasionally brave Velthar-Prime to strip the remaining equipment, but most avoid the beacon's coordinates. Those who investigated reported finding nothing—no wreckage, no bodies, no source for the signal that continues its patient, repeating call. The titanium deposits in the deeper canyons remain untapped, valuable enough to tempt the desperate, but the beacon keeps transmitting, and no one knows who it's calling for.
